description:
Hit repeatedly while filing this session's beads, 2026-07-27. Makes bn writes effectively unusable on Windows without manual intervention.

SYMPTOM: any read (bn status / list / ready) autostarts a daemon which takes the store lock. The next MUTATING command (create / comment / close / sync) then dies with:

  error: store lock already held for <store-id> at ...\store.lock

WORKAROUND, needed before nearly every write: kill every bn process, run 'bn store unlock --store-id <id> --force', then run the write IMMEDIATELY before another read starts a daemon again.

LIKELY CAUSE: the CLI cannot reach the running daemon over IPC and falls back to taking the store lock directly, colliding with the daemon that legitimately holds it. Two tests on this box fail in exactly that area and are probably the same root cause:
  surface::ipc::client::tests::connect_with_autostart_override_waits_for_socket_instead_of_child_exit
  surface::ipc::client::tests::connect_with_autostart_reports_spawned_child_exit_immediately

DANGER WORTH FIXING PROPERLY, not just documenting: 'store unlock --force' does not check whether the lock holder is alive. I force-removed a lock held by a LIVE daemon (pid 6124) and a SECOND daemon (pid 10140) promptly started — two daemons on one store, which is exactly the split-brain the lock exists to prevent. No corruption resulted (store verified: 20 records intact, reads consistent), but that was luck, not design. --force should at minimum refuse, or loudly warn, when the recorded pid is still running.

Related: daemon::runtime::store::lock::tests::acquire_reclaim_rechecks_path_before_remove and the two stale_* lock tests also fail on this box — the lock reclaim path is undertested here in general.
title: bn on Windows: a read autostarts a daemon that then blocks every write
